intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. Encounter howler monkeys, coatis, morpho butterflies, and vibrant poison dart frogs while a naturalist guide explains the intricate relationships within this biodiverse ecosystem.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four monkey species, two-toed sloths, white-nosed coatis, and stunning scarlet macaws, then unwind on the park's pristine white-sand beaches framed by lush jungle — a perfect blend of wildlife and beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek & Jungle Cooking Experience
experiences.description: Venture into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest, home to tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and scarlet macaws. End the adventure with a local guide-led cooking session featuring traditional Costa Rican 'casado' using fresh jungle herbs and ingredients sourced from the surrounding community.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport's casual food court or a soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort if still open — budget $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance (around $10–15 USD) rather than a taxi to save money. Have some colones or USD cash ready for tips and small expenses on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the immediate shoreline, watch local birds, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local farmers market or 'feria' to pick up fresh tropical fruits like mangoes, pineapples, and papayas for snacks throughout the trip. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach, swimming, and spotting coastal wildlife such as pelicans, frigatebirds, and hermit crabs.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or town center for dinner. Find a local 'soda' (traditional Costa Rican eatery) and enjoy a classic Casado plate (rice, beans, salad, plantains, and protein of your choice).

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit from a street vendor or the resort's basic breakfast option — budget $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh tropical fruits and snacks from the local market — budget $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Casado at a local soda restaurant — budget $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to rest and acclimate. Pick up a local SIM card at a nearby tienda (store) for affordable data — Kolbi and Claro are popular budget options around $10–15 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and surrounding coastal trails. Look for howler monkeys, coatis, and tropical birds in the trees near the resort. Bring binoculars if available — many budget hostels and hotels lend them for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group tour or self-guided visit to a nearby mangrove estuary or nature reserve. Explore the ecosystem by foot or rent a kayak (around $10–15 USD/hour) to paddle through mangroves and spot caimans, herons, and iguanas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Cook a simple meal using market ingredients in a hostel kitchen if available, or head back to a local soda for dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans) with eggs at a local soda — budget $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from the market or a beachside 'fritanga' (fried food stand) — budget $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda — arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) or fish of the day — budget $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and reef-safe sunscreen. Bring insect repellent for mangrove areas. February is dry season in most of Costa Rica, so expect sunny and warm weather.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (e.g., Carara National Park or Manuel Antonio, depending on resort location). Arrive early for the best wildlife sightings — scarlet macaws, sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, and caimans are common.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park trails. Enjoy a picnic lunch on a secluded beach or shaded rest area inside the park. Swim in designated beach zones if available.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via shared shuttle or local bus. Relax and freshen up. Head out for a budget dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Bread, peanut butter, and fresh fruit packed from the market — budget $3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch: sandwiches, fruit, and water — budget $4–5 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda near the resort — ceviche and rice or a fish plate — budget $7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: National park entrance fees are typically $18–20 USD per person. Book tickets online in advance to avoid sellouts. Hiring a local guide ($20–30 USD split among a group) dramatically improves wildlife spotting success.

day_by_day.morning: Budget zip-lining adventure! Book a group zip-line tour at a local eco-adventure park near the resort area. Many operators offer packages starting at $35–55 USD including multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and rappelling. Arrive early for cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole for a refreshing dip. Many are accessible by a short hike from the zip-line area. Bring water shoes if possible.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your adventure day with a slightly splurge-worthy dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — try fresh grilled fish or shrimp with patacones (fried plantains). Still budget-friendly by Costa Rican standards.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto and fresh juice at a local soda before the tour — budget $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Snack bar at the eco-adventure park or packed lunch — budget $5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant — grilled fish with sides — budget $10–14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Compare zip-line operators online and look for combo deals that include multiple activities. Always check safety certifications. Wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or stretching on the beach (free or low-cost community classes are common in tourist areas). Follow with a leisurely swim and snorkeling session — rent basic snorkel gear for $5–10 USD and explore the coastal reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or shared ride to a nearby town for cultural exploration. Visit the local mercado (market), browse handcrafted souvenirs, and interact with locals. Look for artisan crafts, hammocks, and coffee — all great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event, local music performance, or simply enjoy a beach bonfire if permitted. Grab street food from a local vendor for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate from a beachside vendor — budget $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Market food stalls — empanadas, tamales, or chorreadas (corn pancakes) — budget $3–5 USD
meals.dinner: Street food — grilled corn, bocas (appetizer-style snacks), and a cold Imperial beer — budget $5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling is best in calm morning waters. Bring a reusable water bottle to reduce plastic waste and save money on drinks throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day eco-adventure: take a guided nature hike through a local cloud forest or rainforest reserve. Look for poison dart frogs, toucans, morpho butterflies, and orchids. Many community-run reserves offer affordable guided hikes for $10–20 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hike or take a break at a scenic viewpoint for lunch. Spot wildlife in the forest canopy and learn about local medicinal plants from your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat yourself to a relaxing evening — soak tired feet, journal your experiences, and organize photos. Opt for a simple, home-cooked style meal.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with fresh fruit and coffee at a local bakery — budget $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the market — rice and bean wrap, fruit, and water — budget $4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda — traditional olla de carne (beef and vegetable stew) — budget $6–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear long pants and long sleeves for jungle hikes to protect against insects and sun. Apply insect repellent with DEET. Leeches are rare but possible — tuck pants into socks.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird-watching walk. Costa Rica is one of the world's top bird-watching destinations with over 900 species. Hire a local birding guide for a half-day session ($20–30 USD) or join a free community walk if available in the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and enjoy a lazy beach afternoon. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) rental for $10–15 USD/hour or simply body surf in the waves. Collect shells and observe beach wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget night wildlife tour ($20–30 USD) to spot nocturnal creatures like tree frogs, kinkajous, and sleeping birds. These guided tours are an unforgettable eco-adventure experience.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh orange juice at a local soda — budget $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Beachside 'casado' or a fresh coconut with snacks from a vendor — budget $5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Post night-tour meal at an open-air restaurant — rice, beans, and grilled chicken — budget $7–10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Bring a red-light flashlight for the night tour to avoid disturbing wildlife. February evenings can be warm but bring a light layer for comfort during the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby sea turtle nesting or hatching beach (if in season — leatherback turtles nest Feb–April on Pacific coast). Join a community-run, certified eco-tour to observe responsibly ($25–40 USD). This is a bucket-list wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the turtle beach — explore the shoreline, take a guided walk, and learn about marine conservation efforts from local rangers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening cooking with fresh ingredients from the market or dining at a local soda. Share stories and photos from the day.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the early tour departure — banana, peanut butter, and coffee — budget $2–4 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or local food near the turtle reserve — budget $5–7 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda — vegetarian casado or seafood option — budget $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Always use certified, responsible turtle tour operators. Never use white flashlights on the beach — use only red lights. Photography restrictions apply during nesting — follow guide instructions strictly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local coffee or chocolate (cacao) farm for a budget tour ($15–25 USD). Learn about the farm-to-cup process, taste freshly roasted coffee and artisan chocolate, and support local sustainable agriculture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby butterfly garden or frog sanctuary ($10–15 USD). These small eco-attractions offer incredible close-up wildlife encounters with poison dart frogs, glass frogs, and dozens of butterfly species.
day_by_day.evening: Head into town for a casual evening. Browse local shops for last-minute gifts and souvenirs. Enjoy a budget dinner and try a traditional 'agua dulce' (hot sugarcane drink) or 'horchata.'

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee at a local panadería (bakery) — budget $3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the coffee or cacao farm (often included or available at low cost) — budget $5–8 USD
meals.dinner: Local soda or market food stall — budget $6–9 USD

day_by_day.notes: Buy locally sourced coffee and chocolate directly from farms for the best prices and to support small producers. Vacuum-sealed coffee bags travel well and make great souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Adventure day: white-water rafting on a nearby river (Class II–III rapids are great for beginners and budget travelers). Group tours typically cost $45–65 USD including equipment, guide, and a basic lunch. Book through a reputable local operator.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, relax at a riverside picnic area or natural hot spring (if in a volcanic region). Many public hot springs are free or very low cost compared to resort spas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — try 'corvina' (sea bass) or 'pargo' (red snapper) fresh from the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the rafting adventure — gallo pinto, eggs, and fruit — budget $5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Included riverside lunch from the rafting operator or packed snacks — budget $0–5 USD
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant — fresh fish with sides and a cold drink — budget $10–14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear clothes you don't mind getting soaked. Secure all valuables in waterproof bags provided by the operator. Sunscreen should be applied before the tour — reapplication is difficult on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning — enjoy a final leisurely swim, beach walk, or sunrise yoga session. Reflect on the journey and take in the natural beauty of the Costa Rican coastline one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any local attractions or spots you may have missed during the trip. Consider a final snorkeling session, a visit to a tide pool, or a walk through a local botanical garden (often free or very low cost).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable meal at a well-reviewed local restaurant. Try a traditional Costa Rican dessert like 'tres leches' cake or 'arroz con leche' (rice pudding). Pack bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a local café — gallo pinto, eggs, fresh juice, and coffee — budget $5–8 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh ceviche or a fish taco from a beachside stand — budget $6–9 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local restaurant — try the chef's special or a seafood platter — budget $12–18 USD

day_by_day.notes: Start packing early and double-check all belongings. Keep important documents, electronics, and valuables in your carry-on. Confirm your airport transfer or shuttle booking for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — wake up early, enjoy a last cup of locally grown Costa Rican coffee, and take a short final walk on the beach or through the resort grounds. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort by the designated time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport via pre-booked shared shuttle or local bus. Arrive at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute coffee, rum, or chocolate gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight and say 'Pura Vida' to Costa Rica — carrying unforgettable memories of eco-adventures, incredible wildlife, and the warmth of Costa Rican culture.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto and coffee at a local soda or the resort — budget $4–6 USD
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a packed snack for the journey — budget $5–10 USD
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Keep some colones or USD for airport taxes or last-minute expenses. Costa Rica charges a departure tax which is usually included in modern airfare — confirm with your airline. Leave a review for any local guides or small businesses that made your trip special.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront room, and unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport café or convenience store upon arrival – save appetite for Day 2

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance. Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access upon arrival. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for small purchases. The resort is approximately 1–2 hours from the airport depending on location.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to orient yourself, breathe in the ocean air, and get acquainted with the resort grounds and amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local town or beach village for a gentle orientation stroll. Browse local sodas (small family-run restaurants), pick up any essentials, and enjoy the laid-back Costa Rican 'Pura Vida' atmosphere. Dip your toes in the Pacific Ocean for the first time.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace or beach. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant to ease into your trip without over-committing on your first full day.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – included or ~$12–$18 USD
meals.lunch: Local soda near the beach – try gallo pinto (rice and beans), casado, or fresh ceviche (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby mid-range seafood restaurant – grilled fish or shrimp with plantains (~$20–$30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Drink plenty of water to stay hydrated in the tropical heat. Apply sunscreen generously – the equatorial sun is intense. Confirm bookings for upcoming tours and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Tour. Meet your certified naturalist guide at the park entrance. Explore the park's lush trails with a high-powered spotting scope to observe sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and Jesus Christ lizards up close in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the eco-tour through Manuel Antonio's secondary and primary forest trails leading to the iconic Playa Manuel Antonio. After the tour concludes, spend free time relaxing on the white-sand beach inside the park, swimming in the calm turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Freshen up and head to a popular local restaurant in the nearby town for dinner. Stroll the main strip and enjoy the lively but relaxed evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~$12–$18 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack purchased near the park entrance – fresh fruit, sandwiches, or a quick soda meal (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the resort – try arroz con mariscos (seafood rice) or fresh tuna (~$18–$28 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – book your guided eco-tour and park entry tickets well in advance. Wear lightweight, breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes for the trails. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle. The park is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the resort. Optional early-morning birdwatching walk on the resort grounds or nearby nature trail – Costa Rica's Pacific coast is home to scarlet macaws, toucans, and dozens of hummingbird species. Grab binoculars from the resort if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session on the ocean organized through the resort or a local outfitter. Alternatively, take a boat tour to a nearby estuary or mangrove system to spot crocodiles, herons, and roosting birds in a different ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the coastline – a popular mid-range activity that often includes snorkeling, dolphin watching, and an onboard drink. Return at dusk for a beachside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local bakery – fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and coffee (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant or resort pool bar – fish tacos, ceviche, or a burger (~$12–$18 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant – grilled whole snapper or lobster with local sides (~$22–$32 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise in advance through the resort concierge or a local tour operator. Bring a light layer for the evening sea breeze. Snorkeling gear is usually provided on catamaran tours. Check sea conditions before kayaking.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart early by shared shuttle or private transfer toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours depending on starting location). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's diverse landscapes – from coastal lowlands to highland forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna / Arenal area. Check in to a mid-range lodge or use as a base. After settling in, visit La Fortuna Waterfall – a stunning 70-meter cascade in the rainforest. Hike down the steep trail (about 500 steps) for a refreshing swim in the natural pool at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Arenal hot springs (Tabacón, Baldi, or Eco Termales) – natural volcanic thermal pools surrounded by lush jungle. A perfect way to relax muscles after the day's travel and hiking. Dine at a local La Fortuna restaurant afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~$12–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or restaurant stop en route – casado or rice and beans (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Local La Fortuna restaurant – try beef tenderloin in chimichurri or pasta with local vegetables (~$15–$25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: La Fortuna Waterfall charges a small entrance fee (~$18 USD). The trail is steep and can be slippery – wear proper footwear. Hot springs range from budget ($15 USD) to luxury ($85+ USD) – Eco Termales is a great mid-range option with a more intimate atmosphere. Book hot springs in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike – Trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor. Spot poison dart frogs, toucans, howler monkeys, coatis, and stunning views of Arenal Volcano on a clear morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges tour, explore the Arenal Volcano National Park base trails for closer volcanic views and additional wildlife spotting. Visit the Arenal Observatory Lodge viewpoint for panoramic volcano photography.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a free evening. Browse the town's souvenir shops, enjoy a local craft beer at a brewpub, or take a night walk tour to spot nocturnal wildlife including tree frogs, kinkajous, and insects.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast or La Fortuna café – gallo pinto, eggs, and fresh juice (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch or restaurant near the hanging bridges – sandwiches, fruit, and juice (~$10–$14 USD)
meals.dinner: La Fortuna town restaurant – wood-fired pizza or Costa Rican fusion cuisine (~$15–$25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park is one of the best options for the hanging bridges experience. Morning visits offer the best wildlife activity and clearest volcano views before clouds roll in. Wear layers as the forest can be cool and misty. Bring a rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart La Fortuna by shared shuttle or jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal toward Monteverde (approximately 2.5–3 hours). The iconic jeep-boat-jeep route is a scenic adventure in itself, crossing the lake by boat with volcano views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde / Santa Elena. Check in to your mid-range lodge. Visit the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve or the Monteverde Butterfly Garden for a gentle introduction to the cloud forest ecosystem. Spot resplendent quetzals if lucky – February is near their breeding season.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Santa Elena town – browse artisan shops, local galleries, and cheese shops (Monteverde is famous for its dairy). Enjoy dinner at a cozy restaurant with mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at La Fortuna lodge before departure (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Café or soda in Santa Elena upon arrival – light meal of empanadas, soup, or a sandwich (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Monteverde restaurant – try local cheese fondue, wood-oven chicken, or a vegetarian dish with cloud forest mushrooms (~$15–$25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer is the most scenic and efficient route from La Fortuna to Monteverde – book through a local tour operator. Roads into Monteverde are unpaved and bumpy – a 4WD vehicle is recommended if driving independently. Temperatures in Monteverde are cooler (15–22°C) – pack a light fleece or jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple cables, Tarzan swings, rappelling, and breathtaking views above the forest canopy. Operators like Extremo or 100% Aventura offer excellent mid-range options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a guided nature walk. Explore the famous 'Elfin Forest' with a naturalist guide to spot orchids, bromeliads, rare ferns, and cloud forest wildlife including the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and emerald toucanet.
day_by_day.evening: Frog Pond of Monteverde night tour – guided walk through a frog sanctuary to spot red-eyed tree frogs, glass frogs, and other nocturnal amphibians. A magical and unique wildlife experience perfect for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and Costa Rican coffee (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Café near the cloud forest reserve – hearty soup, sandwich, or casado to fuel the afternoon (~$10–$14 USD)
meals.dinner: Santa Elena restaurant – try locally produced cheese pizza, pasta, or a hearty stew (~$15–$22 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line canopy tour and cloud forest reserve entry in advance. The zip-line tour requires closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. The Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve has a daily visitor limit. Bring a waterproof jacket – the cloud forest lives up to its name with frequent mist and light rain.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching tour in the Monteverde area – February is an excellent month for spotting the resplendent quetzal as breeding season approaches. A specialized bird guide will maximize your chances of rare sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Depart Monteverde by shuttle toward Tortuguero (a long travel day of approximately 5–6 hours via San José or direct shuttle/boat connections). Alternatively, if the logistics are too complex, this can be a second Monteverde exploration day with the Tortuguero trip moved to Day 10.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tortuguero village. Check in to a mid-range jungle lodge. Enjoy dinner at the lodge and an orientation briefing about tomorrow's wildlife safari. The remote, car-free village of Tortuguero has a wonderfully wild and adventurous atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Monteverde before departure (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Tortuguero lodge restaurant – Caribbean-style rice and beans with chicken or fish, plantains (~$15–$22 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small plane – no roads connect to the village. Most shuttle packages include the final boat transfer from Caño Blanco or Moín dock. Book accommodation and transfers well in advance as Tortuguero has limited capacity. Bring cash as ATMs are unreliable in this remote area.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari – Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari. Spot caimans, river otters, green turtles (in the canals), Jesus Christ lizards, three species of monkeys, manatees, and an extraordinary diversity of waterbirds including kingfishers, herons, and anhingas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero village on foot – visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the park's famous nesting sea turtles (green turtles nest July–October, but the park's ecology is fascinating year-round). Take a self-guided kayak paddle through the smaller canals.
day_by_day.evening: Optional night boat tour through the canals to spot nocturnal wildlife including caimans with glowing eyes, sleeping birds, and tree frogs. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed evening at the lodge listening to the sounds of the jungle.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before the morning safari (~$10–$14 USD)
meals.lunch: Village soda or lodge lunch – Caribbean rice and beans, fresh fish, or plantain-based dishes (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant or village restaurant – coconut curry, jerk chicken, or grilled snook in Caribbean style (~$15–$22 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero's wildlife is most active in the early morning – be ready for a 5:30–6:00 AM departure for the river safari. Wear dark, muted clothing to avoid startling wildlife. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and electronics. Insect repellent is essential in this humid jungle environment.

day_by_day.morning: Second morning canal tour or guided hike through Tortuguero National Park's beach and forest trails. Look for nesting shorebirds, tracks of nocturnal animals, and enjoy the wild Caribbean coastline. The beach itself is stunning and largely deserted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Depart Tortuguero by boat and shuttle back toward the Pacific coast / resort area (approximately 4–5 hours). Enjoy the scenic boat ride back through the canals as a final farewell to the Caribbean jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening, take a swim in the ocean or pool, and have a quiet dinner at the resort after the journey.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure (~$10–$14 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop en route at a roadside soda (~$8–$12 USD)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant – celebrate your return to the coast with fresh seafood and a cocktail (~$20–$30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transfer from Tortuguero the day before. Departures are typically early morning by boat. The journey back involves multiple legs (boat + shuttle + possibly taxi) – stay organized with your luggage and keep valuables accessible. Reconfirm any remaining tour bookings upon return to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Day Trek & Jungle Cooking Experience – Venture into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest. Spot tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and one of the densest jaguar populations in Central America. Note: This requires an early departure (travel to Osa Peninsula may require an additional transfer or domestic flight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado experience with the jungle cooking component – learn to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes using ingredients sourced from the jungle and local farms. A unique cultural and culinary experience deep in the wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Corcovado. If the day trip is too logistically demanding from the resort, substitute with a half-day mangrove kayak tour and a cooking class at a local farm near the resort. Enjoy a celebratory penultimate-night dinner at the best restaurant near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Very early resort breakfast or packed breakfast before departure (~$10–$14 USD)
meals.lunch: Jungle cooking experience meal – traditional Costa Rican food prepared in the forest (included in tour)
meals.dinner: Best mid-range restaurant near the resort – splurge slightly on your second-to-last night with a surf and turf or whole grilled fish (~$25–$38 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance booking and a certified guide by law. Access is typically via Drake Bay or Puerto Jiménez – a domestic flight (~$80–$120 USD one way) or a 6–7 hour drive. If the logistics from the resort are too complex, consider replacing this with a local wildlife tour or a day trip to Carara National Park, which is closer to many Pacific coast resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take a final swim in the Pacific Ocean. Pack, check out, and store luggage with the concierge if your flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local artisan market – pick up handcrafted jewelry, locally grown coffee, cacao products, or wildlife-themed artwork. Enjoy a final Costa Rican lunch at a beloved local soda you discovered during your trip.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Pura Vida – zip-lining through cloud forests, paddling jungle waterways, and encountering Costa Rica's extraordinary wildlife.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – savor it! (~$12–$18 USD)
meals.lunch: Favorite local soda or beachside restaurant – one last casado, ceviche, or fresh coconut (~$10–$15 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or café before departure (~$12–$20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight and airport transfer the evening before. Allow extra time for traffic – San José can have significant congestion especially on weekday afternoons. Declare any agricultural products at customs. Keep your favorite Costa Rican coffee in your carry-on to avoid any issues. Pura Vida!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Paddle through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river otters, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. Encounter howler monkeys, coatis, morpho butterflies, and vibrant poison dart frogs while a naturalist guide explains the intricate relationships within this biodiverse ecosystem.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Tour
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most beloved national park with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter all four monkey species, two-toed sloths, white-nosed coatis, and stunning scarlet macaws, then unwind on the park's pristine white-sand beaches framed by lush jungle — a perfect blend of wildlife and beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek & Jungle Cooking Experience
experiences.description: Venture into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth rainforest, home to tapirs, pumas, harpy eagles, and scarlet macaws. End the adventure with a local guide-led cooking session featuring traditional Costa Rican 'casado' using fresh jungle herbs and ingredients sourced from the surrounding community.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on United flight UA. A private luxury transfer with a bilingual chauffeur will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a chilled welcome amenity (tropical fruit platter, sparkling wine) prepared in your beachfront suite upon check-in.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night room-service spread arranged in advance by the resort: ceviche, plantain chips, artisan cheeses, and a selection of Costa Rican craft beers or fresh-squeezed juices.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer (SUV or van) prior to departure. Resort concierge should be briefed on late arrival. Keep luggage accessible for quick check-in. Rest is the priority tonight — big adventures begin tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort orientation morning. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the Pacific. Meet your dedicated concierge at 10:00 for a personalized trip briefing, resort tour, and activity scheduling session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beachfront wellness session: 90-minute couples or solo massage at the resort spa followed by a guided snorkel or paddleboard excursion along the coastline adjacent to the resort. Spot tropical fish, rays, and coastal wildlife in the warm Pacific waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's infinity bar — sip on a Guaro Sour or fresh mango mojito while watching the sun dip into the Pacific. Elegant welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring Costa Rican fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — gallo pinto, tropical fruit bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty Costa Rican single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch at the resort beach club: grilled fresh catch of the day, avocado salad, and agua de pipa (fresh coconut water).
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — tasting menu featuring locally sourced ingredients: sea bass ceviche, hearts of palm salad, slow-roasted pork with yuca purée, and chocolate-passion fruit dessert. Wine pairing available.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fully acclimate, recover from travel, and plan the remaining itinerary with your concierge. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings and arrange necessary gear.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Eco-Tour (morning slot, 7:00 AM departure recommended). Board a private resort transfer to Manuel Antonio — one of Costa Rica's most beloved national parks. A certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope leads you through lush jungle trails. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and Jesus Christ lizards in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploration of Manuel Antonio's pristine beaches within the park — Playa Manuel Antonio and Playa Biesanz offer calm, turquoise waters for a private swim. Return to resort by 15:30. Refresh and enjoy the resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise arranged by the resort along the Manuel Antonio coastline — champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of the coastline and jungle-covered hills. Watch for dolphins and humpback whales (February is peak season).

meals.breakfast: Early pre-tour breakfast at the resort — energy-packed: granola, tropical fruits, scrambled eggs, and Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch boxes prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed on a secluded park beach under the jungle canopy.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Cantina de Manuel Antonio — an upscale local gem renowned for fresh seafood and traditional Costa Rican recipes elevated with modern technique. Try the lobster in coconut sauce.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio is approximately 20–30 minutes from most beachfront resorts on the central Pacific coast. Wear light, breathable clothing and closed-toe shoes for the park. Bring biodegradable sunscreen and insect repellent. February is dry season — ideal conditions expected.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer departs at 06:00 for Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari (full-day excursion with overnight stay). Fly via private charter or scenic light aircraft from the nearest airstrip to Tortuguero — a remote Caribbean jungle paradise accessible only by air or boat. Arrive by 08:30 and check into a premium eco-lodge (Tortuga Lodge & Gardens or similar luxury jungle retreat).
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided boat safari through Tortuguero's legendary canal network. Expert naturalist guides navigate narrow jungle waterways where you'll encounter green sea turtles (nesting season varies, but river wildlife is year-round), caimans basking on riverbanks, river otters, great green macaws, three-toed sloths, and howler monkeys. Paddle through serene flooded forests in a silent electric boat for minimal wildlife disturbance.
day_by_day.evening: Twilight canoe excursion through the canals — spot nocturnal wildlife including red-eyed tree frogs, caimans illuminated by spotlight, and bioluminescent plankton in the water. Return to eco-lodge for a candlelit dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure, plus light refreshments on the charter flight.
meals.lunch: Fresh Caribbean-style lunch at the eco-lodge: rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, grilled snook, fried plantains, and fresh lemonade.
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge fine dining — Caribbean fusion: jerk-spiced chicken, fresh-caught river fish, yuca fritters, and passion fruit cheesecake. Pair with local craft rum cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Pack a separate overnight bag for Tortuguero — you'll leave main luggage secured at the resort. Bring waterproof bag for camera equipment, light rain jacket, and long sleeves for evening mosquitoes. This is a UNESCO-recognized biodiversity corridor — one of the most extraordinary wildlife experiences in Central America.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn bird-watching walk along Tortuguero beach and forest trails with your naturalist guide (05:30 departure). Over 300 bird species have been recorded here. Watch the sunrise over the Caribbean jungle — a truly unforgettable experience. Spot toucans, herons, kingfishers, and rare great green macaws.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return charter flight back to the Pacific coast and resort by early afternoon. Arrive by 13:30. Spend the afternoon at leisure — resort pool, spa treatment, or private beach relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite dining experience arranged by the resort chef. A personalized multi-course dinner served on your beachfront terrace under the stars — celebrating the halfway point of your journey.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the Tortuguero eco-lodge before departure — eggs, fresh tropical fruit, toast, and Caribbean-style coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon return — ceviche bar, fresh salads, and chilled coconut water.
meals.dinner: Private chef in-suite dinner: lobster bisque, pan-seared mahi-mahi with mango salsa, saffron rice, and a decadent chocolate lava cake with vanilla bean ice cream. Sommelier-selected wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return charter flight timing with concierge. Rest and recovery is important today after two days of intensive wildlife exploration. Tomorrow begins the highland adventure portion of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs at 07:00 toward Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3.5–4 hours from the central Pacific coast). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's lush interior highlands. Arrive at a premium Arenal lodge (The Springs Resort & Spa or Nayara Springs) by mid-morning and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Wildlife Hike. Trek through primary old-growth rainforest on a network of 16 hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor, offering a bird's-eye perspective of the jungle canopy. Your expert naturalist guide identifies wildlife including poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, toucans, and sloths. The iconic cone of Arenal Volcano looms dramatically overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural volcanic hot springs at the resort's private thermal pools as evening falls — the warm mineral-rich waters are perfect for muscle recovery after today's hike. Watch for Arenal's occasional lava glow on the volcano's flanks at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go gourmet breakfast box from the resort before early departure — croissants, fruit, yogurt parfait, and thermos of Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at a scenic overlook during the hanging bridges hike — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water prepared by the lodge.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nayara's Amor Loco restaurant (or equivalent premium resort restaurant) — contemporary Latin cuisine with Arenal volcano views: wagyu beef tenderloin, heart of palm salad, and artisan desserts.

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges experience is moderate difficulty — comfortable hiking shoes and light layers recommended as the cloud forest can be cooler than the coast. Binoculars are essential. February offers excellent visibility on Arenal Volcano.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboard tour on Lake Arenal at sunrise — the glassy lake reflects the volcano perfectly in early morning light. Spot kingfishers, herons, and migratory birds along the lakeshore. Return to lodge by 09:30 for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal region wildlife immersion: private guided afternoon walk through secondary forest trails adjacent to the lodge. Focus on reptile and amphibian spotting — poison dart frogs, basilisk lizards, and fer-de-lance snakes (safely observed). Visit a local butterfly garden and frog sanctuary for a closer look at Costa Rica's extraordinary amphibian diversity.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine and chocolate tasting experience at the resort — featuring Costa Rican single-origin cacao paired with international wines. Followed by a stargazing session with a resort astronomer (February dry season offers spectacular night skies above Arenal).

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast buffet — made-to-order omelettes, tropical fruit station, fresh-baked pastries, and specialty coffee bar.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local open-air soda (traditional Costa Rican eatery) near Arenal — casado (rice, beans, salad, plantains, and protein), fresh fruit juice. An authentic cultural experience.
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining: seven-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing — celebrating the midpoint of the Arenal segment. Highlights include Costa Rican-inspired amuse-bouche, local cheese course, and volcano-view dessert presentation.

day_by_day.notes: Rest day energy should be managed wisely — tomorrow is the most adrenaline-packed day of the trip. Ensure camera batteries are charged and memory cards cleared for the zip-line adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs at 06:30 toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Arenal, partly on scenic mountain roads). Check into a premium Monteverde lodge (El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens). Brief rest and gear preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — the crown jewel of the itinerary. Soar through the mystical misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Multiple cables, Tarzan swings, rappels, and sky bridges offer heart-pounding perspectives of the cloud forest ecosystem 200 feet above the forest floor. Your expert guides ensure maximum safety and excitement. Spot quetzals, toucans, and howler monkeys from the cables.
day_by_day.evening: Adrenaline comedown: a private guided night walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve. The cloud forest transforms after dark — spot glass frogs, tarantulas, sleeping birds, olingo (a rare arboreal mammal), and the elusive kinkajou with your guide's red-light torch.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic Monteverde café upon arrival — local cheese (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), fresh bread, and hearty soup.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Celajes Restaurant at El Silencio Lodge (or equivalent) — cloud forest-inspired cuisine: mushroom risotto with locally foraged fungi, beef tenderloin with chimichurri, and artisan ice cream made with local dairy.

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line participants should wear closed-toe shoes and avoid loose jewelry. Weight restrictions apply (typically 100kg/220lbs max — confirm in advance). The cloud forest temperature is noticeably cooler (15–20°C/59–68°F) — pack a light fleece or jacket. Monteverde's misty atmosphere creates magical photographic conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided early-morning bird-watching walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve (06:00 departure). February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal — one of the world's most spectacular birds. Your expert ornithologist guide uses a spotting scope to locate quetzals, emerald toucanets, and over 400 other cloud forest species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Orchid Garden for an intimate look at cloud forest biodiversity. Afternoon free time to explore the charming town of Santa Elena — browse artisan shops, visit local cooperatives, and sample artisan cheeses at the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería), a community institution since 1953.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer begins the journey back toward the Pacific coast — stop en route at a scenic lookout point for sunset views over the Gulf of Nicoya. Arrive at resort by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before bird-watching — granola, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Full brunch at the lodge upon return from bird-watching — eggs, fresh-baked bread, local cheeses, and tropical fruit.
meals.dinner: Dinner en route at a premium restaurant in the Puntarenas or Jacó area — fresh Pacific seafood: whole grilled snapper, shrimp in garlic butter, and coconut rice.

day_by_day.notes: The road between Monteverde and the Pacific coast involves some unpaved mountain sections — private 4WD transfer is essential. Luggage should be packed and ready by 14:00 for the afternoon departure. This is a transitional travel day — pace activities accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by early morning if the previous evening's transfer ran late, or enjoy a peaceful morning at the resort. Full spa morning: 90-minute deep tissue massage, hydrotherapy circuit, and facial treatment. This is a dedicated recovery and relaxation day after the highland adventures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sport fishing charter from the nearest marina (Pacific sailfish, marlin, dorado, and roosterfish are abundant in February — peak dry season). A luxury yacht with experienced captain and first mate provides world-class offshore fishing. Catch-and-release philosophy encouraged.
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire experience arranged by the resort — private setup on your section of beach with cushioned seating, tiki torches, a personal butler, s'mores station, and live acoustic guitar performance by a local musician.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — leisurely and indulgent after the highland journey.
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the fishing yacht — fresh ceviche made from the morning's catch (if applicable), gourmet sandwiches, cold beers, and tropical juices.
meals.dinner: Resort beach barbecue — fresh catch of the day grilled to order, whole lobster, corn on the cob, and handcrafted cocktails. Served at the private bonfire setup.

day_by_day.notes: Sport fishing charters should be booked at least 48 hours in advance — concierge can arrange. Bring sunscreen, polarized sunglasses, and a light hat for the fishing excursion. February Pacific conditions are typically excellent — calm seas and high visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight or luxury ground transfer departs early for Corcovado National Park (Osa Peninsula) — approximately 45 minutes by light aircraft from the central Pacific coast. Check into a premium Osa Peninsula eco-lodge (Lapa Rios Lodge or Bosque del Cabo) for a one-night stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Corcovado National Park Day Trek & Jungle Cooking Experience — venture into one of the world's most biodiverse places on a guided day hike through Corcovado's old-growth primary rainforest. Your expert guide leads you through ecosystems teeming with Baird's tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. The jungle cooking experience follows: learn to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes using jungle-foraged ingredients alongside a local chef in a stunning rainforest setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a sunset yoga session on the clifftop platform overlooking the Pacific and the Osa Peninsula jungle canopy — one of the most dramatic natural settings imaginable.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — high-energy foods for the trek ahead.
meals.lunch: The jungle cooking experience IS lunch — traditional gallo pinto, hearts of palm salad, plantain dishes, and fresh tropical fruit prepared and eaten in the rainforest.
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge dinner featuring locally sourced Osa Peninsula ingredients: fresh Pacific snapper, organic vegetables from the lodge garden, and tropical desserts. Paired with Costa Rican craft spirits.

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits — concierge must arrange these well in advance. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long pants (for river crossings), and bring a dry bag for valuables. Wildlife encounters here are exceptionally close and frequent — this is widely considered the best wildlife destination in the Western Hemisphere.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wildlife walk on the Osa Peninsula coastal trail with your naturalist guide — spot scarlet macaws in their roost trees at sunrise, sea turtles on the beach, and humpback whales offshore (February is excellent whale season). Return to eco-lodge for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Charter flight back to the central Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive by 13:00. Afternoon at leisure — final resort experiences: private plunge pool time, last spa treatment, or simply relaxing on your beachfront terrace with a good book and a cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the resort's most prestigious dining experience. Private table on the beach set with candles, flowers, and personalized menu. A five-star chef prepares a bespoke multi-course meal celebrating the flavors of Costa Rica's diverse regions: Tortuguero Caribbean, Monteverde cloud forest, Arenal highlands, and Pacific coast.

meals.breakfast: Full eco-lodge breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, local coffee, and homemade bread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon return — chilled gazpacho, grilled vegetable plate, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Private beach farewell dinner: amuse-bouche of Caribbean ceviche, hearts of palm and mango salad, cloud forest mushroom risotto, Pacific lobster tail with truffle butter, artisan Costa Rican chocolate tasting plate, and a bottle of vintage Champagne.

day_by_day.notes: This is the penultimate night — take time to review any souvenir shopping needs with the concierge. The resort can arrange premium artisan gift curation from local cooperatives. Confirm departure transfer and flight details for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — a quiet, reflective moment to absorb the natural beauty of Costa Rica one last time. Optional final spa treatment (book the previous evening). Leisurely checkout — most luxury resorts offer late checkout (12:00 or later) for premium guests; confirm with concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs for Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) — timing based on your return flight schedule. The bilingual chauffeur can stop en route at a premium artisan market or specialty coffee plantation for last-minute authentic Costa Rican souvenirs: single-origin coffee, artisan chocolate, and handcrafted ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and luxury immersion in one of the planet's most biodiverse destinations. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — make it count. Full gourmet spread with everything you loved over the past 13 days: gallo pinto, tropical fruits, specialty coffee, fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a final stop at a quality café near the airport — casado one last time, or a classic Costa Rican tres leches cake.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining (or airport lounge dinner if departure is early evening).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for SJO airport check-in, immigration, and security. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no wildlife products, shells, or plants without proper documentation. Declare all food items. Costa Rica's biosecurity is strict and respected. Safe travels!
